findings.source_quote: εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἐξουσίαν κατέλιπεν αὐτοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν
findings.english_quote: “Repentance” renders the noun metanoia. While it can denote a change of mind, Hermas’s penitential context supports the established church sense of turning back through confession and amendment.
findings.issue: The note adds confession as a specified component of repentance without support in the selected passage. Its appeal to an established church sense also conflicts with the newer contextual decision: Hermas’s own framework, rather than a generic ecclesiastical definition, must control. The main-text “for repentance” is source-compatible.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain “for repentance.” Revise the note to explain moral-spiritual change of disposition and conduct without specifying confession or imposing an established church formula. Preserve the superseded rationale in historical metadata rather than presenting it as current reader guidance.

findings.source_quote: [Ὅσοι, φησί, συμπαλαίσαντες τῷ διαβόλῳ ἐνίκησαν αὐτόν, ἐστεφανωμένοι εἰσίν·]
findings.english_quote: Textual variant: The sentence “Those who grappled with the devil and overcame him are crowned” is bracketed in some editions and absent in some witnesses.
findings.issue: The supplied working source establishes that this clause is bracketed, but the note gives an unattributed claim about omission in witnesses. No supplied report identifies those witnesses or explains whether these brackets mark an editorial supplement or another textual reservation. The note therefore does not adequately disclose the basis and status of the included bracketed text.
findings.suggested_revision: State that the selected Lightfoot & Harmer normalized source prints the clause in brackets. Supply an attributed apparatus or transcription report with locators for the omission claim and bracket significance, or limit the note to what the supplied source establishes. Keep the disclosed working clause rather than replacing it merely because an omission is reported.

findings.source_quote: οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ὑπὲρ τοῦ νόμου παθόντες·
findings.english_quote: The contrast suggests two groups: some suffered (likely to the point of death), others were pressed by trials but neither underwent that ultimate suffering nor denied the law.
findings.issue: The note introduces death as the likely defining distinction and then describes the other group as not undergoing “that ultimate suffering.” The selected source distinguishes suffering from being hard-pressed but does not specify death. The note risks making a proposed interpretation govern the preserved assertion.
findings.suggested_revision: Explain that the source distinguishes those who suffered for the law from those who were hard-pressed without suffering or denying it. If a martyrdom interpretation is retained, label it explicitly as an interpretation not stated by these words and provide its evidentiary basis.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ὄψει ἑνὸς ἑκάστου τὴν κατοικίαν.
findings.english_quote: Or 'and you will see the dwelling of each one.[b][c]'.
findings.issue: This purported alternative repeats the current wording, includes embedded note markers, and reuses marker “a,” which already identifies an unrelated note about the law and Son of God. Marker “b” is likewise reused elsewhere. The resulting collisions prevent unambiguous reader access to the intended disclosures.
findings.suggested_revision: Give current reader notes unique markers and matching anchors. Move duplicated previous-rendering records to clearly identified historical metadata, retaining the history without presenting unchanged wording and embedded markers as translation alternatives.

findings.issue: The final clause of Hermas’s opening speech is omitted. The earlier “I do not understand” conveys his initial perplexity but does not preserve this concluding repetition and its inferential emphasis.
findings.suggested_revision: Restore a concise concluding sentence, such as “That is why I am puzzled.” This proposed wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ὁ δὲ ἄγγελος ὁ μέγας καὶ ἔνδοξος, Μιχαὴλ ὁ ἔχων τὴν ἐξουσίαν τούτου τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ διακυβερνῶν.
findings.english_quote: The great and glorious angel is Michael. He has authority over this people and governs them.
findings.issue: The simplified edition closes the guide’s quotation after the preceding paragraph and presents this paragraph as unquoted narration. In the source, the identification and explanation of Michael remain part of the guide’s answer introduced by “Listen, he says.” This changes speaker attribution.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the Michael paragraph within the guide’s continuing speech, using consistent quotation punctuation across the explanatory paragraphs.

findings.source_quote: ἐπισκέπτεται οὖν αὐτὸς οἷς ἔδωκεν, εἰ ἄρα τετηρήκασιν αὐτόν.
findings.english_quote: Then he visits those to whom he gave it to see whether they have obeyed it.
findings.issue: “Then” presents temporal sequencing where οὖν supplies an inference from Michael’s role in giving the law. The explicit emphatic subject αὐτός is also lost.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “So he himself visits those to whom he gave it, to see whether they have kept it.” Review this proposed wording against the source before adoption.

findings.source_quote: [Ὅσοι, φησί, συμπαλαίσαντες τῷ διαβόλῳ ἐνίκησαν αὐτόν, ἐστεφανωμένοι εἰσίν·]
findings.english_quote: He says, “[Those who struggled against the devil and defeated him receive crowns.] They are the ones who suffered for the law.”
findings.issue: “Receive crowns” changes the assertion that the victors are crowned into an event of receiving crowns. In addition, “He says” translates φησί outside the brackets, although that attribution lies inside the source’s bracketed clause. This blurs the boundary between bracketed material and unbracketed text.
findings.suggested_revision: Preserve the crowned state and the source’s bracket boundary, for example “[Those who struggled against the devil and defeated him, he says, are crowned.]” Arrange the surrounding dialogue punctuation without presenting the bracketed attribution as unbracketed source text. Fresh review is required.

findings.source_quote: εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἐξουσίαν κατέλιπεν αὐτοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν
findings.english_quote: “Repentance” renders the noun metanoia. While it can denote a change of mind, Hermas’s penitential context supports the established church sense of turning back through confession and amendment.
findings.issue: Independently of the standard edition, this note specifies confession without support in the selected passage and imports an established church definition into Hermas’s contextual framework. The simplified main text “so that they could repent” does not itself add that condition.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain contextual repent/repentance wording. Replace the current reader explanation with one describing moral-spiritual change without requiring confession or imposing a uniform ecclesiastical formula; retain the old rationale only as disclosed history.

findings.source_quote: [Ὅσοι, φησί, συμπαλαίσαντες τῷ διαβόλῳ ἐνίκησαν αὐτόν, ἐστεφανωμένοι εἰσίν·]
findings.english_quote: Textual variant: The sentence “Those who grappled with the devil and overcame him are crowned” is bracketed in some editions and absent in some witnesses.
findings.issue: The omission claim is unattributed, and the note does not establish the significance of the selected source’s brackets. It also has no corresponding marker at the simplified bracketed clause, leaving the reader without a direct textual-status disclosure.
findings.suggested_revision: Anchor a note to the simplified bracketed clause. Identify the selected source’s bracketed presentation and provide attributed evidence and locators for any witness-omission or editorial-supplement claim; otherwise restrict the disclosure to the supplied working source.

findings.source_quote: οἱ ὑπὲρ τοῦ νόμου θλιβέντες, μὴ παθόντες δὲ μηδὲ ἀρνησάμενοι τὸν νόμον αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: The contrast suggests two groups: some suffered (likely to the point of death), others were pressed by trials but neither underwent that ultimate suffering nor denied the law.
findings.issue: The simplified edition’s note likewise introduces death as the distinguishing suffering, although this selected clause does not state that limitation. The qualification “likely” does not make “that ultimate suffering” a translation of the source.
findings.suggested_revision: Describe the preserved pressure/suffering contrast without specifying death. Any retained martyrdom proposal should be clearly separated as an interpretation with supporting evidence.

findings.source_quote: εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἐξουσίαν κατέλιπεν αὐτοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν
findings.issue: Marker “a” points to both an unrelated law/Son note and a duplicated previous-rendering note, not to the repentance explanation. Most inherited notes have no simplified-text anchors, and markers “a” and “b” are duplicated. Consequently, the simplified edition does not reliably expose its terminology and source-choice disclosures.
findings.suggested_revision: Rebuild the simplified edition’s note mapping independently: assign unique markers, anchor repentance and textual-status notes to the relevant wording, and keep previous-rendering history outside the current reader-note sequence.

summary: Both editions require revision. The standard main text covers the selected clauses and preserves the difficult identifications and negations, but its reader notes add unsupported specifications and have disclosure defects. Independent review of the simplified text also finds an omitted concluding clause, changed speaker attribution, and altered wording and bracket scope. Contextual repent/repentance and the disclosed bracketed working reading should be retained. This review evaluates the supplied source and metadata; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify editions. All proposed replacements require fresh review.
